extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and applicants preparing or responding to amendments
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures, content, timing, and signature requirements for amendments to patent applications (claims, specification, drawings) during prosecution, reexamination, reissue, and after-allowance stages, as governed by MPEP and 37 CFR. Focus is on entry/non-entry, handling of non-compliant amendments, examiner's amendments, and preliminary amendment rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status identifiers per 37 CFR 1.121(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must use status identifiers as set forth in 37 CFR 1.121(c) (e.g., Original; Currently amended; Canceled; Withdrawn; Previously presented; New; Not entered).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MPEP provides acceptable alternative phrasings (e.g., 'Original Claim'/'Originally Filed Claim', 'Presently amended'/'Currently amended claim', various forms of 'Canceled', 'Withdrawn from consideration', 'Previously amended', 'Newly added', 'Not entered claim'). The Office may accept additional variations if an Office personnel determines the status is accurate and clear. When accepting alternatives, the examiner is not required to correct them by examiner’s amendment, and applicant will not be notified or required to submit corrective compliant amendment; the examiner does not need to state on the record that the alternative identifiers have been accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to drawings (37 CFR 1.84) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any changes to application drawings must comply with 37 CFR 1.84 and be submitted on a replacement sheet (or as a new sheet for additional drawings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement or new sheets must be attached to the amendment document and identified in the top margin as 'Replacement Sheet' or 'New Sheet'. A replacement sheet must include all figures appearing on the immediately prior version of the sheet even if only one figure is amended. Amended figures must not be labeled 'amended'. A marked-up 'Annotated Sheet' showing annotations/changes may be included (and must be supplied when required by the examiner) and should be presented in the amendment or remarks section explaining the changes. An explanation of changes must be presented in the 'Amendments to the Drawings' or the remarks. If drawing changes are not approved, applicant will be notified in the next Office action and must amend the brief/detailed description to be consistent with drawing changes (e.g., when filing a new drawing sheet). Proposed drawing corrections practice has been eliminated: do not submit red-ink proposed changes; proposed corrections treated as non-compliant under 37 CFR 1.121(d). Letters to the official draftsman are no longer required. Drawing submissions made after allowance without changes to spec/claims should be forwarded to the Office of Data Management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's amendments (37 CFR 1.121(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may make examiner's amendments to the specification and claims without paragraph/section/claim replacement to expedite prosecution and reduce cycle time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner's amendments do not need to comply with paragraphs (b)(1), (b)(2), or (c) of 37 CFR 1.121. If a non-compliant applicant amendment would otherwise place the application in condition for allowance, the examiner may enter the non-compliant amendment and provide an examiner's amendment to correct the non-compliance (e.g., incorrect status identifiers). Examples of corrective actions include: (A) providing a claim listing with proper status identifiers in an examiner's amendment; (B) printing the claim listing, crossing out improper status identifiers and writing correct ones as attachment; or (C) correcting improper status identifiers by instructions in an examiner's amendment. The examiner's amendment should include the reason why the amendment is non-compliant and indicate how it was corrected. Authorization from applicant or attorney and extensions are not required if the changes are not substantive (format/typographical corrections). If changes are substantive (e.g., claim cancellation or scope change), authorization and appropriate extensions are required and must be given within the time period for reply set forth in the last Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and handling of non-compliant amendments (PTOL-324)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment fails to comply with 37 CFR 1.121, the Office will notify applicant by a Notice of Non-Compliant Amendment (Form PTOL-324) identifying the non-compliant sections, required items for compliance, and reasons for non-compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form identifies which section is non-compliant (e.g., amendments to the claims section), items required for compliance (e.g., a claim listing in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121(c)), and reasons why it fails to comply (e.g., missing status identifiers). The type of amendment determines whether a response period is provided and whether the applicant's reply must include only the corrected section (e.g., corrected claim listing) rather than the entire amendment. Various amendment types have specific processing rules and timeframes (see separate entries for amendment-type-specific handling).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendment filed after the filing date (non-compliant procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment filed after the filing date that fails to comply with 37 CFR 1.121 will result in TSS sending a Notice of Non-Compliant Amendment with a two-month non-extendable reply period; failure to reply timely results in examination without entry of the preliminary amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No extensions are permitted. Applicant's reply must include the corrected section of the amendment. If no timely reply, the proposed changes will not be entered into the record for examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendment present on the filing date (non-compliant procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment that is present on the filing date but fails to comply with 37 CFR 1.121 will prompt OPAP to send a 'Notice to File Corrected Application Papers' with a two-month reply period; extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to reply may result in abandonment of the application. Applicant's reply is required to include either a substitute specification under 37 CFR 1.125 if the amendment is to the specification, or a complete claim listing under 37 CFR 1.121(c) if the amendment is to the claims. For applications filed prior to certain dates, preliminary amendments present on filing date may or may not be part of original disclosure (see separate entry on original disclosure/timeliness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-final amendment including RCE (non-compliant procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-final amendment (including an amendment filed as a submission for an RCE) that is non-compliant will result in TSS sending a Notice of Non-Compliant Amendment with a two-month reply period; extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to reply to the notice will result in abandonment of the application. Applicant's reply is required to include the corrected section of the amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: After-final amendment (non-compliant procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: An after-final amendment that is non-compliant will be forwarded in unentered status to the examiner; the examiner should indicate any non-compliance in the advisory action and attach a Notice of Non-Compliant Amendment to that action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice provides no new time period for correcting the non-compliance; the existing time for reply from the final Office action continues to run and applicant must still respond to avoid abandonment. If applicant wishes to file another after-final amendment, the entire corrected amendment (not just the corrected section) must be submitted within the time period set forth in the final Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental amendment when no suspension of action (non-compliant procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplemental amendment filed when there is no suspension of action under 37 CFR 1.103(a) or (c) will be forwarded to the examiner and is not entered as a matter of right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner will notify the applicant if the amendment is not approved for entry; the examiner may use form paragraph 7.147. See MPEP § 714.03(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental amendment filed within a suspension period (non-compliant procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplemental amendment filed within a suspension period under 37 CFR 1.103(a) or (c) that is non-compliant will result in TSS sending a Notice of Non-Compliant Amendment with a two-month non-extendable reply period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No extensions of time are permitted; failure to submit a timely reply will result in the application being examined without entry of the supplemental amendment. Applicant's reply is required to include the corrected section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment filed in response to a Quayle action (non-compliant procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment filed in response to a Quayle action that is non-compliant will prompt TSS to send a Notice of Non-Compliant Amendment with a two-month reply period; extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to reply will result in abandonment. Applicant's reply is required to include the corrected section of the amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: After-allowance amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 (non-compliant procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: An after-allowance amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 that is non-compliant will be forwarded to the examiner; such amendments are not entered as a matter of right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner will notify the applicant if not approved for entry and may attach a Notice of Non-Compliant Amendment (37 CFR 1.121) to form PTO-271. The notice provides no new time period. If applicant wishes to file another after-allowance amendment, the entire corrected amendment must be submitted before payment of the issue fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess claims fee requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendment (including after-final amendments) that adds new claims in excess of the number previously paid for must be accompanied by payment of the required excess claims fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to pay required excess claims fees will result in non-entry of the amendment. See MPEP § 607 for fee calculation and timing guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of amendments with defective directions
rubrics_metrics.description: Directions for entry of an amendment may be defective (e.g., inaccurate paragraph/page/line references or lack of precision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the correct place of entry is clear from context, the amendatory paper will be properly amended in the Technology Center and the examiner will initial the margin, assuming responsibility for the change; the applicant should be informed of the alteration and entry in the next Office action. If defective directions leave doubt as to applicant's intent, the amendment will not be entered and the applicant will be informed of the nonentry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of replacements (amendment of amendments)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a replacement paragraph or section of the specification is to be amended, the replacement should be wholly rewritten and the original insertion canceled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A marked-up version of the replacement paragraph/section should be presented using underlining to indicate added subject matter and strike-through to indicate deletions. Matter canceled by amendment can be reinstated only by a subsequent amendment presenting the canceled matter as a new insertion. A claim canceled in its entirety may be reinstated only by a subsequent amendment presenting the claim as a new claim with a new claim number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments in reexamination and reissue proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments in reissue applications and reexamination proceedings must comply with the specific CFR provisions governing those proceedings (e.g., 37 CFR 1.173 for reissue; 37 CFR 1.530 for ex parte/inter partes reexamination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In patent-owner-filed ex parte reexaminations, the patent owner may amend at the time of the request in accordance with 37 CFR 1.510(e). No amendment or response may be filed between the date of the request for ex parte reexamination and the order for ex parte reexamination (37 CFR 1.530(a)). Following the order and prior to the examination phase, an amendment may be filed only with the patent owner's statement under 37 CFR 1.530(b). During the examination phase, amendments may be filed (A) after the first examination as specified in 37 CFR 1.112, (B) after final rejection or an appeal has been taken if the amendment meets the criteria of 37 CFR 1.116, and (C) when and as specifically required by the examiner. See MPEP §§ 2250, 2266, 2666.01, 2672, and 1453 for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirements for amendments (37 CFR 1.33)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments and other papers filed in the application must be signed by a person having authority to prosecute the application; unsigned or improperly signed amendments are not entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per 37 CFR 1.33: signers include a patent practitioner of record, a patent practitioner not of record acting under 37 CFR 1.34, or the applicant. For juristic entities, papers must be signed by a patent practitioner. An amendment signed by only one of joint inventors without appropriate power of attorney is not entered. When an unsigned/improperly signed amendment is received it will be listed in the file contents but not entered; the examiner will notify applicant and advise furnishing a duplicate properly signed amendment or ratify the amendment; in an application not under final rejection, applicant should be given a two-month time period to ratify (37 CFR 1.135(c)). An amendment signed by a practitioner suspended/excluded from practice is not entered and will be submitted to the Office of Enrollment and Discipline. A registered attorney/agent not of record acting under 37 CFR 1.34 may sign. An amendment signed by the applicant (not attorney) in an application with a duly appointed attorney may be entered and acted upon; copies should be sent to the attorney and applicant. Amendments submitted on behalf of a juristic entity must be signed by a patent practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendment content and publication compliance (37 CFR 1.121/1.115/1.215/1.125)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any preliminary amendment, whenever filed, must comply with 37 CFR 1.121 (e.g., include a complete listing of all claims and each section must begin on a separate sheet) and must be in a format usable for publication if the Office is to publish it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary amendments transmitted in a transmittal letter will not comply. If a preliminary amendment to the specification (other than claims) is filed in a format unusable for publication, OPAP will require the applicant to submit a substitute specification in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121(b)(3) and 1.125. Only a substitute specification is usable for publication as an amendment to the specification. Preliminary amendments to claims or the abstract in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121(c) and 1.121(b)(2) can be published without a substitute specification. Applicants should avoid preliminary amendments when possible, incorporating desired changes into the original specification and claim set at filing to avoid publication and processing issues; including a new claim set as part of the originally filed specification may avoid application size fees since both the specification and preliminary amendment count toward page limits per 37 CFR 1.16(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and original disclosure status of preliminary amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment is one received on or before the mail date of the first Office action; its status as part of the original disclosure depends on filing date and applicable rule dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed on or after September 21, 2004 (effective date of 37 CFR 1.115(a)(1)), a preliminary amendment present on the filing date is part of the original disclosure. For applications filed before that date, a preliminary amendment present on the filing date is part of the original disclosure only if referred to in the first executed oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.63 filed in the application. A preliminary amendment filed after the filing date is not part of the original disclosure. Preliminary amendments should accompany the application or be filed after the application has its application number and filing date so they include appropriate identifications (application number and filing date). Any amendment filed after the mail date of the first Office action is not a preliminary amendment; if receipt date is later than the mail date and the amendment is not responsive, the Office will not mail a new Office action but will advise applicant the amendment is nonresponsive and that a timely, responsive reply must be filed to avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds and timing limits for disapproval of preliminary amendments (37 CFR 1.115)
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment compliant with 37 CFR 1.121 will be entered unless disapproved by the Director; disapproval grounds include cancellation of all claims without presenting new/substitute claims or undue interference with preparation of a first Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A preliminary amendment cancelling all claims without presenting new claims will be disapproved. Factors for undue interference include the state of preparation of a first Office action at receipt date and the nature of changes to spec/claims that would result from entry. Entry will not be disapproved if filed no later than: (i) three months from filing date under 37 CFR 1.53(b); (ii) filing date of a continued prosecution application under 1.53(d); or (iii) three months from date national stage is entered per 1.491 for international applications. The specified time periods are not extendable. If filed after these periods, disapproval may be appropriate when the examiner has devoted significant time to preparation of the Office action and entry would require significant additional time; supervisory approval is required for denying entry when filed after the time periods.
